persistence_note: wfi-auditor-b is read-only by charter and holds no write tool, so it returned this body and the orchestrating session wrote it to disk verbatim. No check result, severity, finding, or proposed revision was altered.

checks.finding: All four required elements present and independently verified. (1) Metric row named: Target-Metric: gate_reports.total, matching the retrospective's 'Quality-Gate Runs' column; confirmed reports/runs/RUN-20260729T235825Z-epic-136-phase4-mcp.json actually contains gate_reports.total: 1, first_pass_gate.passed_first_try: 1. (2) Baseline=1, Target='equal to that retrospective's retained Quality-Gate Runs total (5 for a 5-task feature; the point is agreement, not a fixed number)'. (3) Horizon='next completed feature retrospective (Wave 8b, issues #133/#134)' -- one feature-cycle named. (4) Threshold stated: Verification Plan step 1, 'Agreement is the target; disagreement in either direction is a miss,' plus three supplementary criteria (Data Completeness, retrofit-commit search, Minor-line audit). No missing element.

Evidence scale is not isolated: FP-01 documents 3 distinct consumer failures across 8 artifacts and all 5 tasks in this feature, and the Retention Check records the same root-cause bucket recurring across WFI-003, WFI-005 and WFI-010 simultaneously this period (all three set Status: Regressed 2026-07-30), each of which had already gone through a prior Applied/Verified cycle -- a widespread, multi-period pattern, not a 1-feature/1-ticket-type isolated friction. Against that scale, a detailed, several-sentence widening of one existing AGENTS.md subsection (8 named fields, per-consumer line citations, one negative rule) is proportional in size and effort -- it neither restructures major workflow files nor amounts to a single sentence or one checklist item. Whether this size of change is mechanistically sufficient to survive the recurrence pattern it responds to is a separate question, addressed under FEASIBILITY-WITHOUT-PLUGINS (Critical, FAIL); that finding does not change this check's own PASS, which evaluates size-to-evidence proportionality only.

Proposed Change lists exactly one target file, AGENTS.md, widening the 'Evidence report identity fields' subsection WFI-003 (Status: Regressed) originally added. No Verified WFI edits the same subsection, so there is no direct text-overwrite conflict. But a scan of all Verified WFIs found a real interpretive conflict: WFI-008 (Status: Verified, 2026-07-19) states 'do NOT edit or regenerate the 21 evidence bundles or their contracts -- rewriting Done-task evidence to reach PASS is the exact tampering class the threat model defends against (docs/THREAT-MODEL.md, "Agent modifies evidence")'; docs/THREAT-MODEL.md:136 independently states quality-gate reports are 'immutable artifacts... the authoritative record.' WFI-020's widened rule text ('must carry... all as bare lines') is not scoped to reports authored from the change date forward -- nothing in Proposed Change, Expected Effect, or Rollback-Plan exempts already-Done, evidence-frozen reports. This is not hypothetical: repository-wide, 66/135 (49%) of existing reports/quality-gate/*.md files lack a bare 'Task:' line and 61/135 (45%) lack 'Run ID:' under the CURRENT, narrower rule -- a large body of frozen evidence the widened rule's plain text does not exempt. WFI-010's own Result section shows this exact tension was already litigated once: 'The epic-136-phase1-guards period's six gate reports remain non-compliant on the main branch history; their retroactive correction is a separate human decision' -- i.e. established practice here is NOT to retrofit frozen evidence, but WFI-020 does not say so, leaving room for a future agent to read the widened rule as retroactive and retrofit Done-task evidence, contradicting WFI-008's Verified disposition.

The Expected Effect cannot plausibly be achieved by the AGENTS.md-only Proposed Change, because the WFI's own Root Cause Hypothesis correctly diagnoses the primary metric's failure mode as plugin-side, and independent verification found the WFI's own investigation missed the concrete evidence of this. (a) WFI's own diagnosis: 'the quality-gate skill's own authoring step... never cross-references [AGENTS.md]... freely-authored (no separate template file exists for this report)... A rule that lives only in a file the authoring agent is not reading at write time is, operationally, invisible' -- verified verbatim at plugins/sdd-quality-loop/skills/quality-gate/SKILL.md:201-202. Proposed Change touches only AGENTS.md, so it cannot close this diagnosed gap; widening invisible content from 2 fields to 8 does not make it visible. (b) The SKILL.md claim is factually false: plugins/sdd-quality-loop/templates/quality-report.template.md exists, and its first three lines are literally 'Task ID: {{task_id}}', 'Feature: {{feature}}', 'VERDICT: {{verdict}}'. It was updated by WFI-005 (commit c3a7a16d, 2026-07-08) and remains guarded by a passing parity test (tests/template-validator-parity.tests.sh, re-run during this audit: 10 passed, 0 failed). No skill or script under plugins/sdd-quality-loop/ references this template (grep confirms 0 hits) -- it is a maintained, valid, orphaned artifact. The false 'no template exists' SKILL.md text was introduced in commit 825d6c66 (2026-07-19), 11 days AFTER the template was extended and 7 days after WFI-005 VERIFIED 100% compliance using it (epic-136-phase1-guards, 6/6 reports, 0 retrofits) -- the false claim was written after the true fix already existed and had already been proven to work. (c) Repository-wide field-compliance data (135 reports/quality-gate/*.md files) confirms template-backed fields are complied with far more reliably than AGENTS.md-only fields: Task ID:/Feature:/VERDICT: (template-backed) 134/135, 133/135, 134/135; versus Task:/Run ID: (AGENTS.md-only, no template) 69/135 and 74/135 (49% and 45% missing); Critical:/Major:/Minor: (specified nowhere) 80/135 each. This is a natural experiment inside the WFI's own evidence base showing the mechanism it proposes to extend already has an empirically ~50% failure rate, while the mechanism it declines to touch (plugin template + parity test) has ~99% success. (d) The duplicate 'Task ID:'/'Task:' requirement the human author flagged as possible ceremony is the unreconciled residue of two prior WFIs picking different field names on two sides of the project/plugin boundary -- WFI-003 (project-side, chose 'Task:') and WFI-005 (plugin-side template, chose 'Task ID:'); emit-run-record.sh:129 greps only 'Task:', check-evidence-bundle.sh:201 greps only 'Task ID:'. Reconciling those two plugin scripts to accept one canonical field would retire the duplicate line entirely; WFI-020 instead makes the duplication permanent because its Proposed Change cannot touch plugin scripts. The plugin-side fix this WFI defers to 'the plugin's own backlog... tracked... via the wfi-audit-cycle GitHub Issue this WFI produces' will not in fact be produced: plugins/sdd-quality-loop/skills/wfi-audit-cycle/SKILL.md STEP 8 creates a GitHub Issue only for Category: plugin-improvement and explicitly skips (GitHub-Issue: N/A) for Category: app-dev-efficiency; it has no branch for Category: measurement, so WFI-020's 'GitHub-Issue: Pending' will not resolve under the current orchestrator implementation. Expected Effect requires a behavior change that can only be durably achieved by modifying plugin files (SKILL.md's authoring-step cross-reference and/or the template + a validator). The WFI is architecturally misclassified for its own stated durability goal; either the Category should be plugin-improvement with a narrowed project-side change (and Meta-Change: true preserved, as the WFI itself already anticipates), or the Proposed Change must be revised to target genuinely project-side mitigations and the Expected Effect must be scoped down to match what an unenforced AGENTS.md rule has ever actually achieved in this repository.

Category: measurement with a Proposed Change touching only a project-side file (AGENTS.md). Per wfi-category-guide.md Section 1: 'Language rules follow the underlying target (generic if plugin-side, concrete if project-side).' The underlying target is project-side, so Section 3's specificity rules govern, not Section 2's generic-substitution rules. Root Cause Hypothesis and Proposed Change carry abundant concrete detail: feature slug epic-136-phase4-mcp; task IDs T-001..T-005; named scripts and exact line numbers (check-evidence-bundle.sh:201,228; emit-run-record.sh:125,129; generate-evidence-bundle.sh:249-256, all verified accurate at those lines); commit hashes 7b7faa23 and 9e82fa5b (both verified to exist and match their described content); the AGENTS.md rule quoted verbatim (verified word-for-word). No genericization occurred in the Cycle-1 revision; consistent with Cycle 1's own auditor_a_fail_ids, which do not include CATEGORY-LANGUAGE-MATCH.

The target (zero retrofit commits; full gate_reports.total agreement) on the very next completed feature is optimistic given this repository's own track record for the identical mechanism (an AGENTS.md 'must carry' rule with no template or validator backing): WFI-003's original 'Task:'+'Run ID:' rule achieved compliance once (local-env-mcp, Verified 2026-07-06) then regressed; WFI-010's remedy (b) -- the same 'restore AGENTS.md/WFI-003 compliance in authoring' strategy WFI-020 now extends -- achieved 3 consecutive compliant features (epic-159-pillar-a/-b/-c, Verified 2026-07-21) then regressed again this period. A single-feature horizon risks reading a lucky pass or unlucky miss as a definitive verdict on a mechanism with this oscillating history. Separately, the named horizon (Wave 8b, issues #133/#134) was independently confirmed via `gh issue view 133`/`134` to be two documentation-only issues (both labeled `documentation`: #133 is a cross-model failure-policy documentation fix, #134 is authoring THREAT-MODEL.md), so the sample is likely small. gate_reports.total has no risk-tier precondition (unlike WFI-009's stalled cross-model horizon), so it remains technically observable at low N, but a target requiring perfect agreement, measured once, on a small documentation-only sample, is a fragile basis for a Verified/Regressed call in either direction.

Category: measurement, with a Proposed Change naming only a project-side target file (AGENTS.md). Neither of this check's two defined branches (plugin-improvement / app-dev-efficiency) literally applies. Per wfi-category-guide.md Section 1, a measurement WFI's process behavior follows its underlying target -- project-side here -- aligning with app-dev-efficiency's 'No GitHub Issue is created' outcome. This also matches actual orchestrator behavior: plugins/sdd-quality-loop/skills/wfi-audit-cycle/SKILL.md STEP 8 creates an issue only for Category: plugin-improvement and explicitly skips for Category: app-dev-efficiency; it has no branch for Category: measurement, so it does neither for WFI-020, leaving GitHub-Issue: Pending unresolved. Recorded as SKIP rather than FAIL because this is a process gap, not a WFI content-quality defect -- but it materially affects FEASIBILITY-WITHOUT-PLUGINS: the WFI relies on 'the wfi-audit-cycle GitHub Issue this WFI produces' to track its deferred plugin-side fix, and that issue will not be produced as currently scoped.

Meta-Change: true, forced by Category: measurement. (1) Weakening check: the Proposed Change widens AGENTS.md's rule from 2 required bare lines to 8 plus a new negative uniqueness rule -- every direction is stricter, not looser; no gate, grader, threshold, or audit criterion is relaxed. (2) Non-decreasing guard: the Proposed Change's only target file is AGENTS.md; it adds or removes zero scripts, tests, gates, or deterministic checks (0 before, 0 after touched) -- flat, satisfying the guard (though see FEASIBILITY-WITHOUT-PLUGINS: adding zero deterministic enforcement is a durability concern, not a Goodhart-weakening one). (3) Self-grading check: Target-Metric gate_reports.total is computed by plugins/sdd-quality-loop/scripts/emit-run-record.sh, confirmed untouched by the Proposed Change (only AGENTS.md is listed) -- the verification instrument is independent of what this WFI modifies.

proposed_revisions.change: Add an explicit scoping sentence: 'This rule applies to quality-gate reports authored from the date this change lands forward. Already-Done, evidence-frozen reports -- including the 4 non-compliant reports in this feature and the 66/135 repository-wide reports lacking a Task: line -- are out of scope and must not be edited retroactively, consistent with WFI-008's Verified evidence-immutability policy.'
proposed_revisions.rationale: Resolves the UNINTENDED-CONSEQUENCES Major finding by removing the interpretive gap that could otherwise be read as license to retrofit Done-task evidence, which WFI-008 (Verified) and docs/THREAT-MODEL.md explicitly prohibit.

proposed_revisions.change: Correct the claim 'The quality-gate report has neither [a template nor a validator]' -- a template (plugins/sdd-quality-loop/templates/quality-report.template.md) already exists, already carries Task ID:/Feature:/VERDICT:, and is still parity-tested, but is unreferenced by plugins/sdd-quality-loop/skills/quality-gate/SKILL.md:201-202, which falsely claims no template exists. Either (a) reclassify Category to plugin-improvement (keeping Meta-Change: true per the WFI's own fallback language) and add plugin-side targets: correct the false SKILL.md claim, point step 15 at the existing template, and extend the template plus its parity test to cover Task:, Run ID:, Critical:, Major:, Minor: -- or (b) if Category stays measurement/project-side-only, narrow Expected Effect to acknowledge the fix is a partial, likely-non-durable stopgap given the ~50% historical compliance rate of unenforced AGENTS.md-only fields versus ~99% for template-backed fields.
proposed_revisions.rationale: Resolves the Critical FEASIBILITY-WITHOUT-PLUGINS finding by aligning the fix with the actual, evidence-confirmed root cause rather than deferring it to a GitHub Issue mechanism that will not be created under Category: measurement.
